title: 3.3.0 release: CI green on every OS
description: The release candidate c298ac59 (main e22f5011 plus the version bump) failed CI run 38299118105: windows-latest selftests (nine files: invariants, audit_lookup, py_launch, stamp_verification, check-committed-pii, orchestrator-state, sweep-selftests, and two suites over the 300s budget) and the ubuntu 'report is interactive' hostile-content leg. 3.2.0 was green on Windows, so these are regressions from P122-P124 work that never ran on Windows CI, and they hold the release.
desiredOutcome: CI on the 3.3.0 release candidate is green on ubuntu, macOS and windows: every selftest file passes on windows-latest within the sweep's budget, and the report's hostile-content check passes, with no fix weakening what a check asserts.

tasks.title: The report's tables never widen the page on hostile content, and phase titles do not split mid-letter
tasks.description: CI run 38299118105 (release commit c298ac59, same tree as main e22f5011 plus the version bump; ci/p123 run 38298210727 at e22f5011 failed the same jobs), job 'manifest validation', step 'The report is interactive': FAIL hostile content (planted per table: phases [prose in 1 cell(s), token in 0 bare + 0 full-width + 1 evidence-mark cell(s)] + data [prose in 1 cell(s), token in 1 bare + 0 full-width + 0 evidence-mark cell(s)] + data bugs [prose in 1 cell(s), token in 1 bare + 0 full-width + 0 evidence-mark cell(s)] + data [prose in 1 cell(s), token in 1 bare + 0 full-width + 0 evidence-mark cell(s)]) widens the document at no width: got 833px (818 -> 849), want none. This is a regression from P123.90 (d434414), which added `.content :where(table){overflow-wrap:break-word}` after `.content{overflow-wrap:anywhere}` split phase titles mid-letter at 833px. `break-word` does not lower a cell's min-content width, so a planted unbroken token in a table cell widens the document again - the check `tools/check-report-interactive.mjs` (hostile content leg) exists for exactly that. Find a rule that satisfies BOTH: no table cell token widens the document at any width (the hostile leg), and ordinary phase titles in a wide table do not break mid-word when there is room (the reason P123.90 added the exception) - e.g. `anywhere` on the cells that carry free text with the title column given a min-width, or table-layout fixed on the tables whose columns are known; read the refactoring-the-assembled-ui skill and budget pins (`python3 tools/count-ui-pins.py`). Verify with `node tools/check-report-interactive.mjs` on the committed example AND the live plan render AND the hostile leg the CI step runs (read .github/workflows/ci.yml for its exact invocation). Re-render committed artifacts (examples/report.sh; docs/demo-large.html per check-rendered-artifacts.py) and do NOT recapture screenshots - the orchestrator does.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test_render_report.py: the report CSS carries the rule that keeps a table cell's unbroken token from setting the table's minimum width

tasks.title: py-launch.sh parses under Git's sh on Windows for every spelling of $0
tasks.description:
CI run 38299118105 (release commit c298ac59, same tree as main e22f5011 plus the version bump; ci/p123 run 38298210727 at e22f5011 failed the same jobs), windows-latest, test_py_launch.py: FAIL pl20 a `$0` spelled with backslashes and NO slash (what Git's sh on Windows is handed) still names the launcher's directory - read as 'run from the cwd' it looked for the hook beside the cwd, found none and prompted on a healthy install: {'out': '', 'err': "hooks\py-launch.sh: -c: line 114: syntax error: unexpected end of file from `case' command on line 65
", 'code': 2} | FAIL pl21 ...and an ABSOLUTE all-backslash `$0` (a drive letter on Windows) resolves from another working directory too: {'out': '', 'err': "<outside-repo> -c: line 114: syntax error: unexpected end of file from `case' command on line 65
", 'code': 2} | FAIL pl22 ...and a `$0` mixing the two separators resolves the same: {'out': '', 'err': "hooks\.\py-launch.sh: -c: line 114: syntax error: unexpected end of file from `case' command on line 65
", 'code': 2}. All three fail with the same shell syntax error ('-c: line 114: syntax error: unexpected end of file from `case' command on line 65'), so the launcher text the test hands to Git's sh does not parse there - most likely a line ending (a CR left in the script as written or as read), a backslash inside a case pattern that Git's sh reads differently, or a quoting difference under `sh -c`. Find which by reading py-launch.sh's case at line 65 and how test_py_launch builds and invokes the script for pl20-pl22 (P123.24 162c8f03 added them). If the product file itself would fail on a Windows user's machine, that is the fix (py-launch.sh stays POSIX-sh builtins only); if only the test's way of invoking it is wrong, fix the test and say so. It reproduces only on windows-latest; the executor cannot run Windows here, so the fix is reasoned from the CI lines quoted below and the code, kept green on macOS, and verified by the orchestrator's next CI run. State in the return exactly which Windows behaviour the fix assumes, with its source (Python/Git-for-Windows docs or the CI output).

tasks.title: A sweep marker whose pid is dead reads as stale on Windows too
tasks.description: CI run 38299118105 (release commit c298ac59, same tree as main e22f5011 plus the version bump; ci/p123 run 38298210727 at e22f5011 failed the same jobs), windows-latest: FAIL o3 a marker whose pid is dead is reported as stale, never as live (a mutating sweep is live (pid 3024, since 2026-10-12T20:02:18Z) - the tree is mid-mutation, do not read a gate over it) | FAIL mk2 a marker whose pid is DEAD is ignored - the sweep proceeds - and says that it did: '' / 'sweep-selftests: refusing to start - <outside-repo> says a mutating sweep (pid 2496, since 2026-10-12T20:02:29Z) is rewriting the tree; a run now reads mid-mutation files and reports false reds. Wait for it, or stop it.\n'. Both tools/orchestrator-state.py (o3) and tools/sweep-selftests.py (mk2) read a mutation marker naming a DEAD pid as a LIVE sweep. On Windows `os.kill(pid, 0)` does not probe - signal 0 is not a no-op there (it maps to TerminateProcess / CTRL events) - so a liveness probe written for POSIX is wrong on Windows. Find the one place (or the duplicated places - make them one helper if they are two) that decides pid liveness, and give it a Windows branch using a probe that exists in the stdlib there (e.g. ctypes OpenProcess + GetExitCodeProcess == STILL_ACTIVE), with the POSIX branch unchanged. Grep for every other caller of the same probe in plugins/audit and tools and route it through the helper (fix the class, not the two instances). It reproduces only on windows-latest; the executor cannot run Windows here, so the fix is reasoned from the CI lines quoted below and the code, kept green on macOS, and verified by the orchestrator's next CI run. State in the return exactly which Windows behaviour the fix assumes, with its source (Python/Git-for-Windows docs or the CI output).
